Looting in Maluti

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
looting in Maluti- R2.6 billion rand is owed to Eskom and now they want to switch off the lights but 13 businesses in Harrismith are fighting back

Unique Selling Point:
A herculean court battle ensues at the End of October between several arms of government and 13 businesses in Harrismith which will become a case study for many dysfunctional municipalities across the country

Summary:
In March this year Eskom was about to cut off electricity to the Maluti A Paphong municipality (MAP) but they were stopped in their tracks. 13 businesses in the area went to court to ask for relief. They say It is so unreasonable that no reasonable person could have arrived at the same conclusion

The court granted a temporary solution and prevented Eskom from cutting the power. But at the end of the month the court in Bloemfontein will hear arguments. The incredible thing is that instead of trying to find a solution, government and Eskom are opposing their application. ESKOM, NERSA, The MEC, the Premier of the Free State, and several national departments including the presidency are set for a showdown that could be a case study for many dysfunctional municipalities across the country.


Further information:
Map is a case study of a municipality unable to provide basic services or meet its financial commitments.

Eskom is owed R2.6 billion rand from MAP which has been in financial dire straights since 2011. In fact MAP has been in constant default and ratcheted up the debt of R2.7 billion from 2014 to 2018- in only four years and where the money has gone is currently a mystery.
What we do know is that Vusi Tshabalala, the mayor installed by Ace Magashule was hounded out of the municipality earlier this year. He has about 20 cars, as many shiny suits and was listed as one of the recent plotters in Durban against Cyril Ramaphosa. He is currently trying to get back into the council.


The businesses court papers are more than one thousand pages. But in summary they argue:
There were no efforts by the Department of Public enterprises to address the current crisis
Organs of state remained stoicly silent as the crisis unfolded
The businesses (Applicants) were left completely in the dark
There was no intergovernmental attempts to resolve or address the crisis
No one has given them the information they have asked for, like how the debt was calculated;h ow long Eskom had known there was a problem; how had Eskom tried to enforce compliance, what steps were taken by Eskom and NERSA to amend MAPS license conditions; the details of Maps ability to repay the amount of R2.6 billion
Details of all engagements by Nersa to find a long term solution which is less draconian and destructive than the solution currently threatened by Eskom
What the MEC's did to solve the problem, what did the ministers did to solve the problem

They say that none of this information has been provided and instead Eskom selects a one dimensional blunt instrument to the exclusion of all others and chooses to punish the public for the failures of Eskom and the various spheres of government.

Should the businesses lose they say it will be catastrophic for an important rural transport node between Gauteng and KZN. The decision would punish ordinary consumers who had complied and been paying their bills and would effectively shut down the businesses and there would be a massive job loss. They say the decision is both irrational and unlawful.

Carte Blanche goes to Harrismith and Qua Qua to investigate.

Script:


Final Script Looting in Maluti TX Sunday 21st October 2018

Commentary One
For many of us Harrismith is just a pit stop on the N3, but this Free State town is also home to big businesses, which have invested hundreds of millions of rands here. Nestle for example, makes baby food for the entire African continent.

Up Sound AFGRI

Next door AFGRI have recently spent well over a hundred million rand on this state of the art facility that turns wheat into flour.

Around the corner millions more is invested in carpet manufacturing, and just outside town Coca-Cola's plastic bottles are taking shape. Nearby, around 12 000 school jerseys are made every day.

But all of this investment and the jobs that go with it, hang in the balance, because Maluti A Phofung, the municipality which should supply basic services to the town, has failed dismally to do its job.

Ben Deysel
It's got to the stage where the municipal council has come to the businesses to ask for us to prepay our electricity, so they can pay salaries! So where does the money go?

Up sound truck

Commentary Two
Ben Deysel spent 20 years building Highway junction in Harrismith. It is the largest truck stop in Africa, but his business and the future of Harrismith itself, is in jeopardy, because Maluti A phofung never paid over the money they received for electricity to Eskom, and Eskom will cut the power if they don't get paid

LINK
Think of a million rand, multiply it by 1000 and then 2.7 That is right R2.7 billion rand! That is the massive debt to Eskom that this municipality has racked up in the last four years

Mahlomola Majake
This municipality has collapsed. Absolutely collapsed

Commentary three
Mahlomola Majake is the leader of the opposition in Maluti A phofung, based here in Puthadijhaba, about 50 kilometres from Harrismith. MAP as it's known, is responsible for services to 4400 square kilometres of the eastern free state.

Mahlomola Majake
This municipality used to have investments and savings, come Vusi era. Pvttt! gone!

Commentary four
The Vusi era, was nearly five years of Vusi Tshabalala as Mayor of Maluti A Phofung. A man
deployed by former premier of the Free state, Ace Magashule, and said to be his lackey

Mahlomola Majake
Even when the chap was talking, he will talk like Ace, he will make actions like Ace,
He will show some authority just like ACE normally does. When he was talking he will always do like Ace does

Commentary five
Tshabalala soon earned himself a reputation as a man with a penchant for the good life

Paratlane Motloung
Vusi was leading this extravagant lifestyle, he owns a lot of cars, luxury cars, you know. He is that type of a person

Commentary six
Paratlane Motloung spent nine years in the council on an ANC ticket, but by 2011 his anti- corruption stance saw him cast out in the political wilderness. Now he is back as an official at MAP, trying to fix some of the damage done during the former Mayor, Vusi Tshabalala's era

Paratlane Motloung
He would organize festivals instead of doing service delivery

Up sound Ntsa, Ntsa, Ntsa

Commentary seven
Festivals that would cost millions, says Majake who is also chair of the municipal public accounts committee

Majake
On every public holiday there was an event

Commentary eight
But still Eskom's bill remained unpaid

Derek
How would you say Vusi Tshabalala played a role in this staggering debt to Eskom and the implosion of the municipality?
Paratlane Motloung
He basically interfered in the administration. He would even instruct people who to pay who not to pay. I am made to understand that whenever the municipality received its equitable share he would come back from wherever he went so he would come and direct how it would be expended.


Commentary nine
Each month millions of rand's were collected at registered vendors for prepaid electricity which should have been paid over to MAP. But instead Vusi Tshabalala closed them down and opened his own network

Derek
During this time the whole method of collecting prepaid electricity was changed? What happened there?
Ben
It was a total disaster! all the legal appointed suppliers of electricity were kicked out, the previous mayor opened a little spaza shop downtown where you could only buy prepaid electricity on a cash basis, and all that money just disappeared

Commentary ten
And when the province should have intervened, they didn't.

Derek
During this time, we had Premier Magashule, what did he do to ensure good governance?
Paratlane Motloung
As much as he is my Secretary General in the ANC, I don't think he helped the situation at all, because the guy who was the former mayor Vusi was very close to the SG of the ANC, there was a lot of complacency

Ben
The municipality and the mayor took instructions from the province, and from Mr. Magashule, so there was a very close relationship, and it was almost like the municipality was managed from Bloemfontein

Commentary eleven
Then in December 2017, with an Eskom debt into the billions, the municipality went on an unexpected employment drive. 470 people got jobs, another 136 were promoted

Paratlane Motloung
They were captured as employees on the 14 of December, the following day they were paid when they had not even lifted a finger to do any work for the municipality

Commentary Twelve
Their allegation is that SOME of the people got jobs to vote at NASREC for NDZ

Majake
The deal was to go and vote for NDZ.
Paratlane
Also, I was active in the campaign of Cyril Ramaphosa then, so I have reason to believe they were meant to vote for Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma



Commentary thirteen
But the minister rejects the allegation.

Minister Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma
I don't know anything about that for a start, if it happened obviously it was wrong. Is it possible to get almost 500 delegates from one municipality when the entire province had the same number of delegates? So, something doesn't make sense

Commentary Fourteen
Her office later confirmed the entire Free State only sent 324 people to the conference

Up sound protests

Commentary fifteen
The beginning of this year brought chaos. Pensions hadn't been paid over, and staff were on strike. When the municipality removed the people Majake calls the NASREC staff, they attacked the administrators

Up sound police siren

Guns were drawn. MAP had become like a movie, he says

Majake
Yes, it was the Italian job in Maluti A Phofung! That municipality a lot of things happen, it was an action!

Commentary sixteen
On the streets residents demanded Tshabalala must go, inside the chamber the opposition moved to oust him, even some of his own councilors wanted him out. But Tshabalala seen here banging on the desk in a rage was determined to stay.

Up sound Cell phone footage

With no choice really, Minister of Co-operative governance, Zweli Mkhize put MAP under administration, and said there will be consequences for transgressors

Minister Mkhize
Maluti A phufong, indeed that is quite a challenge. We sat with them and a number of other mayors and municipal managers to indicate our displeasure on the performance of the municipality

Mahlomola Majake
They only came here when it was hot in the kitchen. It was too late, it was too, too late!

Derek link
Then in March the news came through Eskom was threatening to cut the power for up to fourteen hours a day. Catastrophic for the town and of course the corporate sector

Commentary seventeen
13 businesses won an interdict to stop the cuts and pay Eskom directly. But it was just temporary. On Monday they want the Bloemfontein high court to make that permanent - They want nothing to do with Maluti A Phofung, but all levels of government, including Eskom disagree

Derek
So, they are saying you must continue to pay a dysfunctional and mismanaged municipality rather than paying Eskom direct?
Ben
Yes
Derek
And what reasons do they give?
Ben
According to them that is the constitution says and that is the only way they can recover the money. Who from nobody knows! They will never recover the money from the municipality

Commentary eighteen
Eskom referred our questions to Cogta and said they are engaging at ministerial level on this issue. The National energy regulator says they have made a determination on Maluti A Phofung and their document will be published once its finalized.

Derek
In the papers it says that Eskom's decision is an irrational act of collective punishment
Ben
It certainly is irrational because how do you force a bankrupt municipality to pay?!

Commentary nineteen
In May, Vusi Tshabalala was recalled by the ANC. We had questions. We went to his home, sent him emails, spoke to him on the phone. But he told us he does not respond to allegations

Up sound Derek
I think its proper you do respond to allegations.

Commentary twenty
Recently the ANC announced Vusi Tshabalala would be returning to MAP as a councillor.

Derek
What happens if the courts find against the business forum?
Ben
We will certainly go to the constitutional court, Derek we have a right to proper services and we will fight for that

THE END 10 32

PROMO ONE 10 seconds
On Monday, the Bloemfontein high court considers a case of 13 Harrismith businesses against a a municipality that hasn't paid Eskom. Now Eskom wants to switch off the power


PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Free state municipality Maluti A Phofung, owes almost R3 billion to Eskom. Eskom wants its money or they'll cut the power, but this could be catastrophic for industry, jobs and turn Harrismith into a ghost town

PROMO THREE 15 seconds
Free state municipality Maluti A Phufong is one of the worst in the country.
Corruption, guns, pepper spray in the chamber - this administration has seen it all

Majake
Yes, it was the Italian job in Maluti A Phofung!

PROMO FOUR 30 seconds
South Africa is desperate for jobs and investment, but they seem to be doing the opposite down in Harrismith. Now business has taken government to court

Derek
So, they're saying you must continue to pay a dysfunctional and mismanaged municipality rather than paying Eskom direct?
Ben
Yes
Derek
And what reasons do they give?
Ben
According to them that is what the constitution says and that is the only way they can recover the money. Who from nobody knows!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): looting in Maluti- R2.6 billion rand is owed to Eskom and now they want to switch off the lights but 13 businesses in Harrismith are fighting back
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A herculean court battle ensues at the End of October between several arms of government and 13 businesses in Harrismith which will become a case study for many dysfunctional municipalities across the country
metadata.Summary: In March this year Eskom was about to cut off electricity to the Maluti A Paphong municipality (MAP) but they were stopped in their tracks. 13 businesses in the area went to court to ask for relief. They say It is so unreasonable that no reasonable person could have arrived at the same conclusion The court granted a temporary solution and prevented Eskom from cutting the power. But at the end of the month the court in Bloemfontein will hear arguments. The incredible thing is that instead of trying to find a solution, government and Eskom are opposing their application. ESKOM, NERSA, The MEC, the Premier of the Free State, and several national departments including the presidency are set for a showdown that could be a case study for many dysfunctional municipalities across the country.
metadata.Further information: Map is a case study of a municipality unable to provide basic services or meet its financial commitments. Eskom is owed R2.6 billion rand from MAP which has been in financial dire straights since 2011. In fact MAP has been in constant default and ratcheted up the debt of R2.7 billion from 2014 to 2018- in only four years and where the money has gone is currently a mystery. What we do know is that Vusi Tshabalala, the mayor installed by Ace Magashule was hounded out of the municipality earlier this year. He has about 20 cars, as many shiny suits and was listed as one of the recent plotters in Durban against Cyril Ramaphosa. He is currently trying to get back into the council. The businesses court papers are more than one thousand pages. But in summary they argue: There were no efforts by the Department of Public enterprises to address the current crisis Organs of state remained stoicly silent as the crisis unfolded The businesses (Applicants) were left completely in the dark There was no intergovernmental attempts to resolve or address the crisis No one has given them the information they have asked for, like how the debt was calculated;h ow long Eskom had known there was a problem; how had Eskom tried to enforce compliance, what steps were taken by Eskom and NERSA to amend MAPS license conditions; the details of Maps ability to repay the amount of R2.6 billion Details of all engagements by Nersa to find a long term solution which is less draconian and destructive than the solution currently threatened by Eskom What the MEC's did to solve the problem, what did the ministers did to solve the problem They say that none of this information has been provided and instead Eskom selects a one dimensional blunt instrument to the exclusion of all others and chooses to punish the public for the failures of Eskom and the various spheres of government. Should the businesses lose they say it will be catastrophic for an important rural transport node between Gauteng and KZN. The decision would punish ordinary consumers who had complied and been paying their bills and would effectively shut down the businesses and there would be a massive job loss. They say the decision is both irrational and unlawful. Carte Blanche goes to Harrismith and Qua Qua to investigate.
